headline: AMD falls 13% in the chip rout, with extra pressure from security and China concerns
summary: AMD shares fell 13.3% to $424.39 in the broad semiconductor sell-off. Reports also pointed to continuing concerns about firmware security and alleged ties to blacklisted Chinese companies weighing on the stock.
why: AMD fell with the rest of the AI chip group on November 20, when the Nasdaq dropped 5.3% and semiconductor stocks posted double-digit losses. Midday market coverage said AMD’s decline was compounded by concerns about firmware security and alleged ties to blacklisted Chinese companies, issues that add regulatory risk at a time when Washington is tightening controls on AI chips.

AMD had gained on November 12, when investors briefly rotated out of Nvidia after Jensen Huang’s resignation and into its competitors, but that rotation reversed as the sell-off broadened to the entire sector.
context: On November 20 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory and wiping out the Nasdaq’s gain for 2026. Semiconductors led the fall, capping their worst week since 2001.
